title: Effective descent and morphism gluing for sheaves of sets along a covering
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], with all fibre products, and let $\{U_a\to U\}_{a\in A}$ be a covering. Work in a universe containing the objects, arrows and index set $A$, closed under the products below [def-weil-size-convention]. For an object $V\to U$, restriction to the slice site $\mathcal C/V$ means $F|_V(W\to V)=F(W\to V\to U)$ for a sheaf on $\mathcal C/U$ [def-pur-localized-ringed-site]. For each $a$ let $F_a$ be a sheaf of sets on $\mathcal C/U_a$ and let $\phi_{ab}:F_a|_{U_a\times_UU_b}\xrightarrow{\sim}F_b|_{U_a\times_UU_b}$ be isomorphisms, including when $a=b$. Suppose $\phi_{ac}=\phi_{bc}\circ\phi_{ab}$ after restriction to each triple fibre product. There is a sheaf of sets $F$ on $\mathcal C/U$ and isomorphisms $e_a:F|_{U_a}\xrightarrow{\sim}F_a$ with $e_b=\phi_{ab}\circ e_a$ on each double fibre product. Moreover, for sheaves of sets $P,Q$ on $\mathcal C/U$, every family of maps $f_a:P|_{U_a}\to Q|_{U_a}$ agreeing on the double fibre products is the restriction of a unique map $f:P\to Q$.

source.place: Tag 04TR, lemma-glue-sheaves (including the gluing datum immediately preceding it); Tag 04TQ, lemma-glue-maps, applied also to the site C/U

proof.text: For $W\to U$ put $W_a=W\times_UU_a$ and $W_{ab}=W\times_UU_a\times_UU_b$, with the displayed projections. The assignments $H_a(W)=F_a(W_a\to U_a)$ and $K_{ab}(W)=F_b(W_{ab}\to U_b)$, with restriction maps induced by fibre products, are sheaves on $\mathcal C/U$. Indeed, for any covering $\{W_i\to W\}$, its base changes cover $W_a$ and $W_{ab}$ by the site axiom; the double intersections are $(W_i\times_WW_j)_a$ and $(W_i\times_WW_j)_{ab}$ by the pullback universal property. Thus their sheaf equalizer diagrams are exactly those of $F_a$ and $F_b$ for those base-changed coverings. Slice coverings and restrictions have the meaning in [def-pur-localized-ringed-site]; the site and sheaf axioms are [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology](1). All these categories and products lie in the stipulated universe [def-weil-size-convention].

source.place: Tag 04TR (lemma-glue-sheaves), compatible-tuples formula; verification of the component sheaves written out

proof.text: Naturality of $\phi_{ab}$ gives two maps $\prod_aH_a\rightrightarrows\prod_{a,b}K_{ab}$: on a tuple $(x_a)$ their $(a,b)$ coordinates are $\phi_{ab}(x_a|_{W_{ab}})$ and $x_b|_{W_{ab}}$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheaf-sets-limits-sectionwise](1) on the small site $\mathcal C/U$ to form their products and equalizer. This gives a sheaf $F$ with $F(W)=\{(x_a)\in\prod_aF_a(W_a):\phi_{ab}(x_a|_{W_{ab}})=x_b|_{W_{ab}}\text{ for all }a,b\}$. The index categories are small (discrete $A$, discrete $A\times A$, and the finite parallel-pair category); the universe bound in the statement supplies their products. Restrictions are coordinatewise restrictions along $W'_a\to W_a$; they preserve the equations by naturality of $\phi_{ab}$, and preserve identities and composition because every $F_a$ is a functor.

source.place: Tag 04TR (lemma-glue-sheaves), displayed compatible-tuples formula and omitted sheaf verification, using sectionwise limits

proof.text: For every $a$, pull the cocycle identity for $(a,a,a)$ back along $U_a\to U_a\times_UU_a\times_UU_a$, the triple diagonal. If $\alpha_a=\Delta_a^*\phi_{aa}$, it says $\alpha_a=\alpha_a\circ\alpha_a$. This is an equality of automorphisms, so cancellation gives $\alpha_a=\mathrm{id}_{F_a}$. This asserts identity only after diagonal restriction; it does not assert that $\phi_{aa}$ is identity on all of $U_a\times_UU_a$.

source.place: Tag 04TR, gluing datum preceding lemma-glue-sheaves; diagonal normalization from its cocycle

proof.text: For $W\to U_a$, let $d_a:W\to W_a$ be the graph of that structural map. Define $e_{a,W}:F(W\to U)\to F_a(W\to U_a)$ by $e_{a,W}(x)=d_a^*x_a$. To construct its inverse, start with $y\in F_a(W)$ and, for each $b$, let $x_b=\phi_{ab}(y|_{W_b})$, evaluated on the object $W_b\to U_a\times_UU_b$ whose first coordinate is $W_b\to W\to U_a$. On $W_{bc}$, the cocycle for $(a,b,c)$ yields $\phi_{bc}(x_b|)=\phi_{bc}\phi_{ab}(y|)=\phi_{ac}(y|)=x_c|$. Hence $(x_b)$ belongs to $F(W)$; write this map as $i_{a,W}$. These formulas use only the slice restrictions of [def-pur-localized-ringed-site].

source.place: Tag 04TR (lemma-glue-sheaves), omitted construction of local isomorphisms, explicit graph inverse

proof.text: The maps just constructed are inverse: $e_{a,W}i_{a,W}(y)=y$ by Step 3 after restricting $\phi_{aa}$ along the graph $d_a$. Conversely, for $x\in F(W)$ pull its $(a,b)$ compatibility equation on $W_{ab}$ back along $W_b\to W_{ab}$ whose $a$ coordinate is the given $W\to U_a$ and whose $b$ coordinate is the existing projection. This gives $x_b=\phi_{ab}((d_a^*x_a)|_{W_b})$, exactly the $b$ coordinate of $i_{a,W}e_{a,W}(x)$. Thus both composites are identities. For an arrow $h:W'\to W$ over $U_a$, write $h_b:W'_b\to W_b$ for its base change. The identity $h_a\circ d'_a=d_a\circ h$ gives $e_{a,W'}(h^*x)=(d'_a)^*h_a^*x_a=h^*d_a^*x_a=h^*e_{a,W}(x)$. For each $b$, naturality of $\phi_{ab}$ and functoriality of restriction give $h_b^*\phi_{ab,W_b}(y|_{W_b})=\phi_{ab,W'_b}((h^*y)|_{W'_b})$, so the $b$ coordinates of $h^*i_{a,W}(y)$ and $i_{a,W'}(h^*y)$ agree. Thus both maps commute with restrictions. They are inverse sheaf morphisms, so $e_a:F|_{U_a}\xrightarrow{\sim}F_a$.

source.place: Tag 04TR (lemma-glue-sheaves), omitted verification that the local maps are natural isomorphisms

proof.text: For $W\to U_a\times_UU_b$, pull the $(a,b)$ compatibility equation of a tuple $x\in F(W)$ back along the graph $W\to W_{ab}$ of both structural maps. The result is $\phi_{ab}(e_a(x))=e_b(x)$ in $F_b(W)$. Since this holds for every test object $W$, the natural transformations satisfy $e_b=\phi_{ab}\circ e_a$ on the double slice, as required.

source.place: Tag 04TR (lemma-glue-sheaves), omitted commutativity of the gluing diagrams

proof.text: For the morphism clause, fix $W\to U$ and $s\in P(W)$. The family $\{W_a\to W\}$ is a covering by [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology](1). Let $t_a=f_a(s|_{W_a})\in Q(W_a)$. On $W_{ab}$, naturality of $f_a,f_b$ and their assumed equality on the double slice give $t_a|=f_a(s|)=f_b(s|)=t_b|$. The sheaf equalizer axiom for $Q$ therefore gives a unique $t\in Q(W)$ restricting to these $t_a$. Define $f_W(s)=t$; this is a function on every section set.

source.place: Tag 04TQ (lemma-glue-maps), equalizer diagram construction, applied to C/U

proof.text: For $h:W'\to W$ over $U$, both $h^*f_W(s)$ and $f_{W'}(h^*s)$ restrict on each $W'_a$ to $f_a(s|_{W'_a})$, by naturality of $f_a$; separatedness of $Q$ for the base-changed covering gives equality. Hence $f$ is a natural transformation. If $W\to U_a$, let $r_a:W_a\to W$ be the projection and $d_a:W\to W_a$ its graph section, so $r_a\circ d_a=\mathrm{id}_W$. The defining amalgamation equation and naturality of $f_a$ along $d_a$ give $f_W(s)=d_a^*r_a^*f_W(s)=d_a^*f_a(r_a^*s)=f_a(d_a^*r_a^*s)=f_a(s)$. Thus $f|_{U_a}=f_a$. Finally any other such map sends $s$ to a section with the same restrictions on every $W_a$; the uniqueness part of the sheaf axiom [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology](1) makes it equal to $f_W(s)$ for every $W,s$.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-NN-097074eb5 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the whole item and all eight steps, re-derived each step by hand, and checked them against Stacks sites.tex. 04TQ is lemma-glue-maps (lines 5638-5671) and 04TR is lemma-glue-sheaves (5823-5896, including the gluing datum before it); the tag-to-label mapping is in tags/tags lines 6263-6264. The statement matches both results hypothesis by hypothesis: a=b is included, the cocycle and the direction e_b=phi_ab e_a are the same, and the morphism clause is 04TQ applied to C/U. Nothing is weakened and no hypothesis is added. Step 1: the component sheaves follow from 00VH(iii) base change in def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology(1). Step 2: the sectionwise equalizer of products is a sheaf by lem-weil-pbc-site-sheaf-sets-limits-sectionwise(1). That node is a Mathlib leaf, so no tool_use is needed. Step 3: restricting the (a,a,a) cocycle to the diagonal gives alpha=alpha^2, so the diagonal pullback of phi_aa is the identity; nothing is claimed off the diagonal. Steps 4-5: I checked the graph maps d_a and (pr_W, W->U_a, pr_b), the cocycle on W_bc, both inverse identities and naturality. Step 6: pulling back along the graph into W_ab gives phi_ab e_a = e_b. Steps 7-8: I checked amalgamation on the base-changed cover, naturality by separatedness, the restriction identity f_W(s)=d_a^*f_a(r_a^*s)=f_a(s), and uniqueness. I tested an empty cover (everything is terminal and the result holds), an identity cover, a non-mono singleton cover with phi_aa not the identity off the diagonal, repeated members and empty section sets. Delivery shape is correct: 0 new nodes, proof_deps equals the union of the step uses, no SGA, no doubled backslashes, and no off-route statements. Mathlib has the IsStack class but no instance for the sheaf pseudofunctor, so the item is not a leaf. The parent det-pe-torsor-comparison-affine (Steps 4-5, main-20261015) uses exactly these two clauses. This is a generic set-sheaf lemma, not a target node, so the base-change and coefficient-category check does not apply.
